judge-football.justification: Usable 7.7: concrete advice (3-4 hoop runs, shrink one run, Hoop G only as tiebreaker), 42-player 2025 board, pre-registered 2026/27 test; effect under one pressure a season and forecast gain vanishes among players who ran the 40. Confounders 8.3: draft slot, weight, alignment, sample size, best-of-14 permutation (p=0.121), nested re-selection, imputation, single-rep reliability 0.41, EDGE vs interior; injuries only touched. Unique 7.4: same formula on drill and game; honest that bend does not translate (0.10); still a null-leaning Combine-to-production link. Terminology 7.6: mostly correct, Hoop G has coach-level definition; some stats shorthand; 'sideways g' not tied to dip-and-rip/ghost rush.

top_changes: Reconcile inconsistent figures (0.18 vs 0.19 for 40-complete subset, 0.57 vs 0.61 true-score effect, 0.32 vs 0.38 across baseline rows); generate in-text numbers from numbers.json keys; state whether raw 3.1 or shrunk 0.8 pressures per season is the headline.
Resolve missing-40 dependence: Hoop G x has-40 interaction or Bayesian partial pooling with class random effect; report interval and implication for +0.10 vs ~0.00 on the 49 players with a 40.
Pre-specified symmetric leave-one-class-out of the whole pipeline with distribution of delta R2 across class-resampled splits; add a placebo outcome such as run-stop rate.
judge-datascience.justification: Re-ran analysis.py with fewer draws; deterministic numbers matched numbers.json exactly, permutation p within MC noise. Strong design: no-tracking baseline (log pick, weight, NGS, EDGE share), leave-one-class-out with refit bootstrap, best-of-14 permutation, nested re-selection, 40-complete subset and multiple imputation, class-intercept mixed model, reliability-corrected effect, pre-registration. Honest: best-of-14 p 0.121, nested p 0.091, forecast gain vanishes on 49 players with a 40. Weaknesses: main effect not distinguishable from chance; every out-of-class R2 interval includes zero; delta R2 +0.103 driven by the 14 no-40 players; numeric inconsistencies between sections; baseline imputation wording.
